subject: health
unitTitle: Media, Technology, and Digital Influence on Health
title: Mastery check: privacy, data, and health information shared online
focus: privacy, data, and health information shared online
essentialQuestion: Who profits when I believe a health claim, and how do I check before I share it?
keyPoints: Health searches, app entries, location, contacts, and messages can reveal sensitive patterns; check permissions, retention, sharing, and deletion before providing information.
Check authorship, expertise, evidence, currency, uncertainty, and incentive before using a health message; confidence, popularity, and testimonials are not substitutes for support.

For privacy, data, and health information shared online, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Take apart three fictional but realistic health posts: identify the claim, the incentive, the evidence actually offered, and what a reliable source says instead. Write the correction you would actually post.
studentTask: Compare two supplied fictional messages about privacy, data, and health information shared online. Build a four-row check for source or author, evidence, date or context, and incentive; then choose the stronger message, cite two details, and state what remains uncertain.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in privacy, data, and health information shared online; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the privacy, data, and health information shared online task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Teardowns may be written, spoken, annotated on printouts, or completed on a supplied four-column template. No account creation, login, or live platform use is required.
extensionChallenge: Apply privacy, data, and health information shared online under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.

Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of privacy, data, and health information shared online in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Explain privacy, data, and health information shared online accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
